fragments.text: Good morning. First, I'd like to thank the organizers of this AI for Information Accessibility Conference for inviting me to present to you today. My presentation is going to be focused on how the public accounts committees in parliaments can harness the digital transformation to provide a better oversight over the government operations. The presentation will include first to highlight what we consider as a key aspect of the digital transformation that will enable the oversight and, most importantly, the use of data and the digital technologies such as AI to improve the way that the parliament works, particularly on its role on the oversight of public finances for the executive. Now, if you look at that particular role, that role usually is executed through parliamentary

And specifically public accounts committees act as a parliamentary world stock over where taxpayers' money is spent. It is therefore important to focus on how the digital technologies as well as the availability of data can actually be harnessed to improve the transparency of these operations. Improving the transparency of these operations will not only increase the oversight but also enhance the public trust in government. Now research has shown that in the eastern and southern African countries the right of access to information really varies. from those where the public accounts committees can only have access to national government departments to the areas where you would find that the public accounts committee has both

fragments.text: The parliamentary committees really would find benefit in engaging in the open government process, which is really open to parliaments as well as the other branches of government. and it supports many of the aspirations of Parliament. For the Executive Branch, for instance, Parliamentary engagement opens up the opportunities for securing legislation that actually enables Executive Branch commitments, resources for implementations, as well as the situation reforms. The next example, if the commitment is to have open data and open data exchange platforms, then the parliament will enable that by opening up the legislation where there is a need. For parliament themselves, from the domestic perspective, it's a mechanism to hear from citizens and civil society between electoral cycles on how they can better serve the people

fragments.text: they represent. These mechanisms will really enable better accountability in the long run. For civil society organization, the parliamentary engagement is a crucial aspect of securing the sustainability of reforms across administrations and political cycles. Some of the options that the parliaments have to engage in open government is really in two aspects. The first aspect is action plan development. An action plan development could be both in the identification, solution mapping and identifying priorities, or through co-creation of commitments with governments. And a number of governments on the African continent are already engaging in this particular aspect. Good examples will be Quebec, Nigeria and Kenya, which are using this form of engagement from the parliamentary perspective. The second aspect is implementation and monitoring of action plans.

fragments.text: And this is really a key aspect and this can be done through legislative action to implement the open government commitments, or through just the legislative oversight of the open government commitments and activities. This would really require that the executive does reporting on the commitments, as well as the activities in those particular commitments. So, in conclusion, we see that digital transformations offers a number of opportunities for public accounts committees to improve their oversight work, and by using these digital technologies to connect and analyze data, engage with citizens and civil society and to collaborate with other stakeholders, Public Accounts Committee can make more significant contribution to transparency and accountability in government. Thank you.
